title: SaaS pricing: how to pick, test, and migrate pricing models (Corey Haines on 99signals)
summary: Corey Haines explains why pricing is the crux of SaaS growth, why early-stage founders should pick one simple price rather than over-engineer, and how to choose a model by anchoring on value metrics. He also covers testing pricing on new customers only and migrating existing users without grandfathering.

principles.text: Pricing is the crux of the business and a major growth lever; traffic and users are worthless if you can't monetize them well.
principles.quote: the price that you charge and the way that you charge it is really like the Crux of the business and like one of the the major keys to growth

principles.text: Don't over-engineer pricing early. Pick one low-enough price (most users wouldn't balk) that still makes buyers weigh the value.
principles.quote: you just pick a price one single monthly price or annual price that's low enough where people uh or like 75 of your users wouldn't have a problem paying for it but it's still high enough to where they have to think about it

principles.text: Early pricing should be competitive with alternatives, not based on cost-plus; a newcomer with fewer features shouldn't price above incumbents.
principles.quote: You don't really want to base it on competitors but you want to pick something that is competitive

principles.text: Choose the pricing model from how customers get value: find one primary and one or two secondary value metrics, then anchor price to them.
principles.quote: finding your value metrics how do people get value out of your products and then you can anchor your price based on the value metrics

principles.text: If each user has a distinct product experience, per-user pricing is a good start; if value doesn't scale with seats (like Stripe), charge on what does.
principles.quote: is the product experience different per user that that signs up for the product under a team account if so then user-based pricing is usually a really good uh starting place

principles.text: Test new pricing on new customers only, for roughly 3 to 6 months, since existing customers are anchored to their old price.
principles.quote: you want to test some new pricing on new customers only for probably about three to six months at first and because this is really like an unbiased view
